newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks trim gains on consolidation.
newsitem.headline: French stocks trim gains on consolidation.

text.p: French shares trimmed their gains in late afternoon on consolidation with dealers saying their rise was overdone after the Socialist win in Sunday's election.

"Everyone was worried the Americans would sell but when they didn't sell in any big volume, the market rose. Then everyone thought the rise was overdone for the day after an election so there has been some consolidation," said one dealer.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index was up 0.73 percent or 18.93 points at 2,602.87 at 1431 GMT. Earlier in the afternoon, it rose more than two percent to hit an intraday high of 2,645.86.
Dealers said the stock market would remain volatile until the new Socialist-led administration's policies became clear.
Best performers were consumer stocks and those with international exposure while investors were selling privatisation shares, particularly in the defence sector and financial sector.
* Defence electronics firm Thomson-CSF, whose sell-off looks doubtful under the Socialists, was off 6.38 percent at 154 francs while retailer Galerie Lafayette was up 6.43 percent at 2,235 francs.
